title: Countably generated images inside a lisse sheaf are lisse
statement: For a finite-type scheme X over a finite field k, a prime l, and an integer-indexed family of lisse native adic sheaves A_n on Xbar, the image of any map from their coproduct to a lisse adic sheaf V is lisse. No Frobenius structure, simplicity, nonzero assumption, or monicity of the individual maps is required.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3 and 7: geometric constituents, two-point curve restriction and local Frobenius powers; geometric socle/Frobenius orbit step in sk-i-dl-general-real.

proof.text: Choose finitely many geometric points over closed points of the irreducible components, using the proved source exists_geometricPoints_specializes. Finite sums and finite images are lisse by the source kernel-cokernel theorem. Their total stalk ranks are bounded by that of V.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3 and 7: geometric constituents, two-point curve restriction and local Frobenius powers; geometric socle/Frobenius orbit step in sk-i-dl-general-real.

proof.text: Enumerate the integer family by natural numbers. Choose a finite initial image maximizing total rank. Each larger finite image contains it monomorphically with equal total rank. Equal ranks at the detecting points make the lisse cokernel zero, so these inclusions are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Every summand factors through the maximal finite image. The universal property of the infinite image and its finite subimage gives inverse comparison maps, hence an isomorphism with that lisse finite image.
